text:
Marathon Petroleum jumped 3.4% today, recovering some ground after a brutal two-week slide of 8.6%. The move came as oil prices stabilized and refined-product inventory levels tightened — gasoline storage at 209 million barrels and diesel at 99 million barrels are notably low, which improves margins for refiners like Marathon that profit when they can convert crude into fuel at good prices. Refineries are running at 94.5% capacity, suggesting strong demand and limited spare production to flood the market.

The stock's rebound also reflects whiplash from geopolitical headlines. Earlier this week, Trump's comments about an imminent Iran settlement sent crude tumbling below $90, which initially hurt refiner valuations — oil at lower prices means less margin cushion. But the narrative shifted as Secretary of State Rubio downplayed diplomatic hopes, and crude has since firmed to $99.64 domestically, removing the worst-case scenario for fuel producers and allowing Marathon to bounce back.
